note: The DAK layer. Every class below is grounded in an artefact committed to smart-base today; `groundedIn` names which, and each class note says what it was read from. L2 exists to hold the three joins that currently survive only as string equality across three file formats -- BPMN pool name to persona title, DMN usingTask href to BPMN task name, and DMN input expression to data dictionary element name. Those joins break silently on a rename. Nothing else here is modelled for its own sake: rule cells stay properties rather than nodes, FHIR canonicals stay URLs, and an edge with no instance in a real file was left out.

groundedIn.detail: 8 participants, 61 tasks, 3 exclusive gateways, 8 start and 8 end events, 70 sequence flows, 10 message flows, 1 sub-process, 0 lanes, 0 condition expressions. The process, participant, task, gateway, event, flowsTo and messageTo classes are the element types this file actually contains -- not the BPMN specification's full element set.

groundedIn.what: A real, committed DMN decision table
groundedIn.detail: 1 decision, 8 input clauses, 4 output clauses, 25 rules, 1 usingTask href into a BPMN. Two of the four outputs are serialised as outputEntry and two as annotationEntry (guidance text, then the L1 reference); trailing empty annotations are omitted rather than serialised empty, so of the 25 rules only 1 carries a citation, 8 carry guidance only and 16 carry no annotation at all. No hitPolicy attribute is present, so `hitPolicy` is optional on decision-table rather than required.

groundedIn.what: Personas as they already exist, and as the DAK model defines them
groundedIn.detail: 22 ActorDefinition instances carrying name, title, type and description. Persona.fsh adds id, ISCO (bound to urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113883.2.9.6.2.7) and a persona type value set. All 8 BPMN participant names match an ActorDefinition `title` exactly, so `performedBy` has a demonstrable instance -- and a demonstrable failure mode.

groundedIn.what: The two DAK logical models that point at these files and model nothing inside them
groundedIn.detail: Both declare `source 1..1 uri` -- a link to a BPMN or DMN file. DecisionSupportLogic carries nothing else at all. This is the gap L2 fills: WHO's own model addresses the file and stops at its boundary, so no query can cross it.

groundedIn.what: The rule that core data elements are referenced, not copied
groundedIn.detail: `canonical 1..1 uri` pointing at a ValueSet, CodeSystem, ConceptMap or logical model. FHIR already has a query layer and a validator for those, so `definedBy` records the canonical URL and this graph re-represents none of their contents.

predicates.note: A BPMN sequence flow, within one participant. The qualifier carries the flow's name where it has one -- 6 of the 70 flows in the lifecycle BPMN do, all of them gateway branches such as "Yes - approved". No flow in that file carries a conditionExpression, so the branch condition exists only as that label. `openQualifier` says the qualifier is free text authored in the BPMN rather than a term from a fixed vocabulary, so a value the ontology has not seen is not a finding.

A BPMN message flow, which by definition crosses participants. Kept distinct from flowsTo because a handoff between two roles is the thing governance and adaptation reviews look for, and burying it among 70 intra-pool flows loses it.

A participant pool is performed by a persona. TODAY THIS IS STRING EQUALITY between the BPMN participant's @name and an ActorDefinition's title, across two file formats with no shared identifier. Renaming either side breaks it silently and nothing reports it. Every instance of this edge must carry a resolutionStatus.

A decision table is invoked by a business rule task. Read from dmn:usingTask/@href, whose fragment is the URL-encoded task NAME rather than the task id -- in the BCG table it is '#if%20the%20client%20is%20due%20for%20a%20bacille%20Calmette%E2%80%93Gu%C3%A9rin...'. It therefore resolves only if that prose is byte-identical in the BPMN, punctuation included. Carries a resolutionStatus.

An input clause reads a data element. Recovered from the input expression's free text, where element names appear either bare ('HIV status') or quoted inside a larger expression ('Today's date - "Date of birth"'). Quoted tokens on the right of a comparison are values, not elements, so extraction is a heuristic and every instance carries a resolutionStatus and the rule that produced it.

A decision rule cites an L1 source. The target is an l1:citation, so this is the edge that joins the L2 and L1 graphs. Grounded, though sparsely: of the BCG table's 25 rules exactly 1 carries a citation in its second annotation entry. The sparseness is the point -- a rule with no citesSource edge is a rule with no stated source, and counting those is the coverage question.

A data element is defined by a FHIR canonical -- a ValueSet, CodeSystem, ConceptMap or logical model, as CoreDataElement.fsh declares. The target is an l1:external-artifact holding the URL. Nothing about the target's contents is copied here; FHIR is its own query layer.

classes.name: Business Process
classes.note: One BPMN file, as a unit. Corresponds to a BusinessProcessWorkflow instance, whose `source 1..1 uri` points at exactly this. Shares its IRI with the l1:external-artifact for the same file: L1 addresses the file and asserts nothing about the inside, L2 supplies the inside, and one artefact keeps one address.
classes.propertyNote: objectives is `1..1 markdown` on BusinessProcessWorkflow but absent from BPMN XML, so it is optional here and populated only when the FSH instance is read alongside the file.

classes.name: Process Participant
classes.note: A BPMN pool: a role that owns part of the process. The lifecycle BPMN has 8 and no lanes at all, so the pool is the only unit of role assignment present. Its @name is the sole link to a persona.

classes.name: Process Task
classes.note: A BPMN task or sub-process. Present as a node because it is what a DMN usingTask href points at and what sequence flows connect; a task with neither would still be included, since omitting it would disconnect the flow graph around it. Sub-processes are tasks with isSubProcess true rather than a separate class -- the lifecycle BPMN has exactly one, 'For each business process'.

classes.name: Process Gateway
classes.note: A branch or merge. Included for connectivity, not for a cross-model edge: a sequence flow through a gateway that had no node would have nothing to point at, and every reachability question over the process would break at the first decision point. The 3 in the lifecycle BPMN are all exclusive.

classes.name: Process Event
classes.note: A start or end event. Same connectivity justification as gateway, plus one of its own: a process's entry and exit points are what make 'is this task reachable' and 'does this path terminate' answerable at all.

classes.name: Decision Table
classes.note: One DMN decision, as a unit. Corresponds to a DecisionSupportLogic instance, which carries an id, an optional description and `source 1..1 uri` -- and nothing whatsoever about the decision itself. Shares its IRI with the l1:external-artifact for the same file, on the same reasoning as business-process.
classes.propertyNote: hitPolicy is optional: the BCG table declares none, and inventing a default would assert something the file does not say.

classes.name: Input Clause
classes.note: A decision table input column. Its expression text is where data element names hide, which is the only reason this is a node rather than a property of the table.

classes.name: Output Clause
classes.note: A decision table output column. The BCG table's four are Care Plan, Guidance displayed to health worker, Annotations, and Reference(s) -- the last described 'Reference for the source content (L1)'. These are column definitions in a decision table, not clinical records: no output-clause edge reaches patient data, and none may. See docs/SCOPE.md.
classes.propertyNote: isReferenceColumn marks the L1 reference column, identified by its description rather than its position -- column order is not stable across DAKs and indexing by it is how this breaks.

classes.name: Decision Rule
classes.note: One row. Its input and output cells are carried as properties, not as nodes: 250 cells in the BCG table alone, none of them the target of a cross-model edge, and turning them into nodes would re-represent the table rather than join it. What the rule needs a node for is its citation edge into L1.
classes.propertyNote: conditions and outputs are arrays of {clause, description, text} preserving the cell's own two fields; DMN puts the formal expression in description and the human-readable gloss in text, and both are worth keeping.

classes.name: Persona
classes.note: A role, defined once and referenced by name from every process that involves it. Read from ActorDefinition instances in input/fsh/actors, whose shape Persona.fsh governs. `title` is the field BPMN pools match on; `name` is the CamelCase identifier and does not match.
classes.propertyNote: isco is a list of codes from urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113883.2.9.6.2.7. Persona.fsh declares `ISCO 0..* CodeableConcept`, but the committed ActorDefinition instances record ISCO in prose inside description instead, so this field is usually empty and should not be read as authoritative. resolutionStatus is `unresolved` on a persona that a process names but no ActorDefinition defines -- the node exists so that the gap is queryable, and carries a title and nothing else.

classes.name: Data Element
classes.note: A named item of information a decision reads -- the data dictionary row. Currently recovered from DMN input expressions, because smart-base ships no data dictionary instance to read from; a node here is therefore a name that was referenced, not a definition that was found. resolutionStatus says which. When a dictionary exists, resolution fills in the rest and the WHO-versus-country diff this class is for becomes possible.
classes.propertyNote: extractionRule records how the name was recovered -- bare expression, or quoted token left of a comparison -- so a wrong guess is auditable rather than anonymous. resolutionStatus is unresolved | resolved | ambiguous, exactly as for an l1:citation, and for the same reason.

deliberatelyOmitted.what: A `writes` edge from output-clause to data-element
deliberatelyOmitted.why: No instance exists. The BCG table's four outputs are Care Plan, Guidance displayed to health worker, Annotations and Reference(s) -- none of them a data dictionary element. Licensing an edge that no committed artefact exhibits would be inventing vocabulary, which is the failure this repository was rebuilt to avoid.

deliberatelyOmitted.what: Nodes for input and output cells
deliberatelyOmitted.why: 250 in one table, none the target of a cross-model edge. They are carried as properties of decision-rule instead.
The class would have no instance: the lifecycle BPMN uses pools only and declares no laneSet. Add it when a DAK ships one.

deliberatelyOmitted.what: Sequence flow conditions as structured expressions
deliberatelyOmitted.why: The lifecycle BPMN has 70 sequence flows and 0 conditionExpression elements. The branch label carries all there is, so it is the flowsTo qualifier and nothing more is claimed.
Presentation. Coordinates answer no question this graph exists to answer.

The relationship between an L1 external-artifact and its L2 elaboration is carried by the two sharing one IRI, and declared once on the class via its `elaborates` field (which the Turtle export renders as rdfs:subClassOf). An instance edge would have had the same node as its source and its target.

deliberatelyOmitted.what: The contents of any FHIR canonical
deliberatelyOmitted.why: ValueSets, CodeSystems, ConceptMaps and logical models have a validator, a publisher and canonical references already. definedBy records the URL. See the corollary in docs/SCOPE.md: graph what has no other query layer, index what does.
